17-13-0303-C(1) Type 1 Narrative & Plans 7 2240 N. Milwaukee Ave., Chicago, IL
Proposed Zoning: § B3-3 Community Shopping District
Lot Area: 14,733 sq. ft.

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant is proposing to develop the subject property with a new six
and seven-story mixed-use building containing approximately 5,538 sq. ft.
of retail space at grade and fifty (50) dwelling units above. The proposed
building will measure 79 ft.-10 in. in height. The subject property is a
Transit Served Location and will be supported by eleven (11) off-street
parking spaces and fifty (50) onsite bicycle parking spaces. Pursuant to Sec.
17-13-0303-D optional Administrative Adjustment and Variation and
pursuant to Secs. 17-13-1003-EE, 17-13-1101-B, and 17-13-1101-D of the
Chicago Zoning Ordinance, the Applicant is seeking to reduce the
residential off-street parking ratio from 50% (25 parking spaces) to 22% (11
parking spaces), reduce the rear setback for floors containing residential
units from 30 ft. to 20 ft.-2 in., increase the floor area ratio from 3.0 to 4.0,
waive the loading berth requirement, and is seeking all relief necessary, as
allowed by the code, for the attached plans.

(A) The Project’s Floor Area Ratio: 58,724 square feet (4.0 FAR)

*The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location based on its
proximity to the CTA Lawrence Bus Route. Pursuant to Sec. 17-3-0403-B, the
Applicant is seeking to increase the Floor Area ratio from 3.0 to 4.0.

(B) The Project’s Density (Minimum Lot Area Per D.U.): 294.66 (blended) square feet
per D.U. — 50 units proposed)

© The amount of off-street parking: 11 parking space

*The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location based on its
proximity to the California Ave. Blue Line Station. Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1003-
EE, the Applicant is seeking to decrease the off-street parking ratio from 50% (25
parking spaces) to 22% (11 parking spaces).

@) _ Setbacks:
a Front Setback: 8 inches
b. Side Setbacks:
West Side: 3-5/8 inches
East Side: 2-1/2 inches
c. Rear Setback: 20 feet-2 inches

*Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1101-B, the Applicant is seeking to reduce the rear setback
for floors containing residential units from 30 feet to 20 feet.

(E) Building Height: 79 feet-10 inches

Sec. 17-3-0308 Criteria for Transit-Served Locations — Supplemental Narrative Zoning Analysis

1, The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location per Sec. 17-10-0102-B
because it is located within approximately 493 linear feet of the California Ave. CTA
Station. The proposed mixed-use building containing retail space at grade and fifty (50)
residential units above will be supported by eleven (11) off-street parking spaces. Pursuant
to Section 17-13-1003-EE, the Applicant is seeking to decrease the residential off-street
parking ratio from 50% (25 parking spaces) to 22% (11 parking spaces).

2. The Applicant’s building design complies with the requirements of Sec. 17-4-0504, and
the Milwaukee Avenue Corridor Design Guidelines. The retail portion of the proposed
building fronts along N. Milwaukee Ave. The proposed front setback is 8 inches. Teh
residential entry to the proposed building will be located on W. Prindiville St. It will be
setback 3-5/8 inches.

3. The Transit Friendly Development Guide defines ‘transit friendly development’ as
development which is oriented towards and integrated with adjacent transit. The proposed
mixed-use building incorporates accessibility and connectivity to mass transit based on its
location near the California Ave. CTA Station. The Applicant believes the development
will improve the subject area for residents and other commuters traveling in the subject
area.

4. The proposed mixed-use building will contain grade level retail space and fifty (50)
residential units above. The proposed building will be supported by eleven (11) off-street
parking spaces and fifty (50) onsite bicycle parking spaces. The Applicant is seeking
administrative approval to permit the off-street parking ratio (22& proposed) for the
residential units pursuant to the TOD Ordinance.

5. The Applicant believes the proposed mixed-use building will provide appropriate density
in the subject neighborhood. More specifically, the project will replace a surface parking
lot with a new mixed-use building offering new retail space along N. Milwaukee Ave. The
proposed residential units will provide additional residential housing inventory to meet
market demand. Based on the subject property’s proximity to mass transit, he Applicant
believes the project provides transit options and otherwise complies with the Travel
Demand Study and Management Plan rules promulgated by the Department of
Transportation by serving an area in need.
